videos.script: boxoffice runs on your machine, in a container, and in production. The code is the same in all three. Some values are not. {{varies}} This lesson sorts out which values those are, and gives each one three sources: a default in the code, an environment variable, and a flag. {{flags}} The flag package parses a command line in a few lines, and it has three habits that surprise people. {{env}} Environment variables are how platforms hand settings to a program. Every value arrives as a string. {{secrets}} Secrets are different. Anybody on the machine can read a command line, so a token never goes in a flag. It goes in a file only its owner can read. {{files}} Then configuration files, a large library, and dot-env files. {{load}} Last, boxoffice reads everything in one function, checks it, and refuses to start if anything is wrong. All the problems at once, before a single port is open.
